source_text:
Οὐκοῦν ἄπερ ἐλέγετο μικροῦ πρόσ-θεν περὶ τοῦ Ἰσμαὴλ, ὅτι δὴ παραλαβὼν νόμον πατρόθεν, τὸν τῆς περιτομῆς, παρεδί-δου ἐγγόνοις τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ, ταῦτα λέγειν ἡμῖν 595 ἔξεστι περὶ τοῦ Ἡσαῦ, ὅτι ὢν παῖς Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ υἱοῦ Ἁβραὰμ, ὃν παρέλαβε νόμον παρά τε τοῦ πάππου, παρά τε τοῦ πατρὸς ἥκον-τα
εἰς αὐτὸν, παρεδίδου καὶ τοῖς παισὶ, καὶ περιέτεμέν που καὶ αὐτὸς τὸν Ἐδώμ· οὐκέτι οὖν ἀσαφές; Πῶς δὲ καὶ υἱοὶ Ἀμμὼν καὶ υἱοὶ Μωάβ; τούτους γινώσκουσί που οἱ φιλοπονώτεροι εἶναι τοὺς υἱοὺς Λὼτ, τοῦ ἀδελφιδοῦ Ἁβραάμ. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα. Ἐτέχθῃ οὖν ἐκ τοῦ Λὼτ, ὅ τε Ἀμμὼν καὶ ὁ Μωὰβ, ἐκάτερος ἐκ τῶν θυγατέρων αὐτοῦ, ὁπηνίκα ὑπονοήσασαι ἔ-ρημον εἶναι τὴν γῆν, οὕτω διασώσασθαι τὸ γένος τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐβουλήθησαν αἱ θυγα-τέρες Λώτ· ἐτέχθη γὰρ τῇ μὲν πρεσβυτέρᾳ ὁ Μωὰβ, ἑρμηνευόμενος ἐκ πατρὸς, καὶ τῇ δευτέρᾳ Ἀμμὼν, ἑρμηνευόμενος ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ γένους. Ταῦτα πάντα εἰρημένα οὐκέτι δυσ-κόλως ἡμᾶς συγκατατίθεσθαι παραπείθει, πάντας τοὺς περιτετμημένους οὕτω καλεῖσ-θαι ὑπὸ τοῦ ἱεροῦ λόγου, μαρτυροῦντος αὐτοῦ Ἱερεμίου καὶ περὶ υἱῶν Μωάβ, καὶ περὶ τῶν υἱῶν Ἀμμὼν, ὅτι ἐν τοῖς περιτετμημένοις κατέλεξε καὶ τούτους. Καὶ μετ' ὀλίγα. Εἰ δὲ καὶ ὠφελείας τινος ἡμῖν προσγίνεσθαι δεῖ ἐκ τῶν εἰρημένων τούτων, οὕτως ἄν τις ὀρθῶς εἴποι, ὡς τὰ πολλὰ γένη τῶν ἀνθρώπων προσποίησιν μὲν ἔχει δικαιοσύνης, καί τινα μὲν ἴχνη φέρειν νόμου Θεοῦ, καὶ σχηματίζεσθαι πως, καὶ ἐπιπλάστως ἐπιμελεῖσθαι ἀρετῆς, μέχρι μέντοι σχήματος αὐτοῖς ἵσταται τὰ τῆς προαιρέσεως, μέχρι προσποιήσεως καὶ τοῦ καθυποκρίνεσθαι, οὐ μέντοι καὶ τέλεον ἐσ-πουδάσαμεν τὴν κακίαν ἐκκόπτειν ἐξ ἡμῶν καὶ τὰ ὀνείδη ἐπ' Αἴγυπτον καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν Ἰ-δουμαίαν. Cap. x, 2. Κατὰ τὰς ὁδοὺς τῶν ἐθνῶν, μὴ μανθάνετε. Τί δὲ μανθάνετε; Νόμον μανθάνετε Θεοῦ, τὸν λέγοντα· Οὐκ ἔσονταί σοι θεοὶ ἕτεροι πλὴν ἐμοῦ, θεοὶ, οἱ οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν οὐκ ἐποίησαν, ἀπολέσθωσαν ἀπὸ προσώπου τῆς γῆς καὶ ὑποκάτω τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
thought_title: Circumcision inherited and the pretense of righteousness
orientation: Gregory is explaining how Jeremiah can call Egypt, Edom, Ammon, and Moab circumcised, and then draws a moral lesson about pretense of righteousness.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the things which were said a little before about Ishmael, that indeed having received the law from his father, the law of circumcision, he was handing it down to his own descendants, these things it is permitted for us to say about Esau, that being a child of Isaac the son of Abraham, the law which he received from his grandfather and from his father coming to him, he was handing down also to his children, and he circumcised somewhere also Edom himself; is it no longer unclear? But how also the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab? These the more diligent know somewhere to be the sons of Lot, the nephew of Abraham. And after a little. Ammon was born then from Lot, and Moab, each from his daughters, at the time when the daughters of Lot, having suspected the earth to be desolate, thus wished to preserve the race of humans; for Moab was born to the elder, being interpreted 'from father,' and to the second Ammon, being interpreted 'the son of the race.' All these things having been said no longer with difficulty persuades us to agree, that all the circumcised are thus called by the sacred word, Jeremiah himself bearing witness both about the sons of Moab and about the sons of Ammon, that he counted also these among the circumcised. And after a little. But if also some benefit must come to us from these things that have been said, thus someone might rightly say, that the many races of humans have a pretense of righteousness, and bear some traces of the law of God, and are shaped somehow, and superficially care for virtue, but up to appearance their choices stand, up to pretense and to playing the hypocrite, but we have not indeed also fully been eager to cut out the evil from ourselves and the reproaches upon Egypt (the Egyptians) and upon Idumea (that is, Edom). Chapter 10, verse 2. According to the ways of the nations, do not learn. But what do you learn? You learn the law of God, which says: There shall not be for you other gods besides me; gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the face of the earth and from under heaven.

pass_b_english: What was said a little earlier about Ishmael, that he received the law of circumcision from his father and handed it down to his own descendants, we may also say about Esau. He was the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, and the law that came to him from his grandfather and his father he also handed down to his children. He himself circumcised Edom. Is this no longer unclear?
And how are the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab circumcised? Those who have studied more carefully know that these are the sons of Lot, Abraham's nephew.

And after a little: Ammon and Moab were born from Lot, each from his daughters, when Lot's daughters suspected that the earth was desolate and so wished to preserve the human race. Moab was born to the elder daughter, and his name means "from a father." Ammon was born to the younger, and his name means "son of my people."

All these things, once said, persuade us without difficulty to agree that all these peoples are called circumcised by the sacred word. The sacred word itself testifies through Jeremiah about the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, that he counted them among the circumcised.

And after a little: If we should gain some benefit from these words, we may rightly say that many peoples of the human race have a pretense of righteousness and bear certain traces of the law of God. They are shaped in some way and superficially cultivate virtue. Yet their resolve stops at outward form, at pretense and hypocrisy. They did not even strive to cut out evil from themselves, as the reproaches against Egypt and Idumea, that is Edom, show.

Jeremiah 10:2: "Do not learn according to the ways of the nations." And what do you learn? You learn the law of God, which says: "You shall have no other gods besides me." "Let the gods who did not make heaven and earth perish from the face of the earth and from under heaven" (Jeremiah 10:11).

problems.quote: we have not earnestly cut out the evil from ourselves
problems.source_quote: οὐ μέντοι καὶ τέλεον ἐσ-πουδάσαμεν τὴν κακίαν ἐκκόπτειν ἐξ ἡμῶν
problems.why: The Greek uses first person plural aorist indicative ἐσπουδάσαμεν ('we have not... made effort'), but the English 'we have not earnestly cut out' loses the aspectual nuance and makes it sound like a simple past failure rather than 'we did not even make an effort to cut out.' More critically, the subject is ambiguous: the Greek shifts to first person, but the English 'we' could mislead about whether this is authorial self-inclusion or a general 'we' = 'people.'
